title: Cohomological approximation bound for a tensor of two morphisms
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $P,K,Q,L\in D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Use the K-flat derived tensor product of [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor], specialized to $R\to R$. Let $\alpha:P\to K$ and $\beta:Q\to L$ be morphisms, and let $n,m,a,b\in\mathbf Z$. Suppose $H^i(\alpha)$ is an isomorphism for $i>n$ and is surjective for $i=n$, and $H^i(\beta)$ is an isomorphism for $i>m$ and is surjective for $i=m$. Assume $H^i(K)=0$ for $i>a$ and $H^j(Q)=0$ for $j>b$. Set $t=\max(n+b,a+m)$. Then the derived tensor morphism
$$\alpha\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}\beta:P\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q\longrightarrow K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L$$
induces an isomorphism on $H^i$ for every $i>t$ and a surjection on $H^t$. No freeness, pseudo-coherence, lower bound, or finite Tor-dimension assumption on the four objects is imposed.

proof.text: In $D(R)$, apply TR1 to choose distinguished triangles $P\xrightarrow{\alpha}K\to C_\alpha\to P[1]$ and $Q\xrightarrow{\beta}L\to C_\beta\to Q[1]$. The long exact sequence gives $H^r(P)\to H^r(K)\to H^r(C_\alpha)\to H^{r+1}(P)\to H^{r+1}(K)$. For $r\ge n$ its first arrow is surjective and its last arrow is injective, by the hypotheses on $\alpha$. Exactness therefore gives $H^r(C_\alpha)=0$. The same argument for $\beta$ gives $H^r(C_\beta)=0$ for $r\ge m$. Thus the cones have upper bounds $n-1$ and $m-1$, respectively.

proof.text: Regard modules as sheaves on the one-point ringed site, as in the tensor functor used in the statement. Choose flat-term K-flat representatives of $Q$ and $K$ using the K-flat resolution theorem. Exact descent of tensoring with a fixed such representative applies on either side. Consequently tensor the first triangle by $Q$ on the right and the second by $K$ on the left. They give distinguished triangles $P\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q\xrightarrow{f}K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q\to C_\alpha\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q\to(P\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q)[1]$ and $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q\xrightarrow{g}K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L\to K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}C_\beta\to(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q)[1]$, where $f=\alpha\otimes1_Q$ and $g=1_K\otimes\beta$. The normalized identifications in exact descent are with the K-flat derived tensor of the statement, including these morphisms.

source.place: Tags 064M and 06Y6, definition-derived-tor and lemma-derived-base-change; exact K-flat descent on both sides as in sites-cohomology.tex Tag 06YU

proof.text: Apply the existing upper-bound theorem to $(C_\alpha,Q)$ with bounds $(n-1,b)$, and to $(K,C_\beta)$ with bounds $(a,m-1)$. The resulting upper bounds are $n+b-1$ and $a+m-1$. Equivalently, $H^r(C_\alpha\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q)=0$ for $r\ge n+b$ and $H^r(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}C_\beta)=0$ for $r\ge a+m$. Since $t=\max(n+b,a+m)$, both third vertices in step 2 have zero cohomology in every degree $r\ge t$.

proof.text: For each triangle $X\xrightarrow{h}Y\to C\to X[1]$ in step 2, the long exact sequence contains $H^{i-1}(C)\to H^i(X)\xrightarrow{H^i(h)}H^i(Y)\to H^i(C)$. If $i>t$, both outside terms vanish by step 3, so $H^i(h)$ is an isomorphism. If $i=t$, the right outside term vanishes, so $H^t(h)$ is surjective. Apply this to $h=f$ and $h=g$.

source.place: Tags 05RS and 0148, long exact cohomology sequence of a distinguished triangle

proof.text: Bifunctoriality identifies $g\circ f=(1_K\otimes\beta)\circ(\alpha\otimes1_Q)=\alpha\otimes\beta$. The natural transformations in the second tensor argument commute with morphisms in the first, and cohomology preserves composition. Hence above $t$ its cohomology map is a composite of two isomorphisms, and at $t$ a composite of two surjections. These are exactly the assertions.
